name: The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology (TPS)
specimen: Voided and instrumented urine, bladder washings, upper-tract specimens
use: Lower and upper urinary tract cytology: voided, catheterised, bladder wash, upper-tract washings/brushings.
Primary purpose: detection of high-grade urothelial carcinoma.
not_use: Not designed to detect low-grade urothelial neoplasms (low sensitivity).
Non-urothelial lesions primarily (renal mass FNA – use kidney system).

adequacy.title: Adequacy
items: Voided: ≥25 mL (ThinPrep) or ≥30 mL (SurePath) recommended volume.
Instrumented: ≈20 well-visualised urothelial cells per 10 HPF (ThinPrep) as guidance.
Any atypical or worse cells → adequate.

categories.name: Non-diagnostic / Unsatisfactory
categories.definition: Specimen inadequate for evaluation of high-grade urothelial carcinoma.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Nikas IP et al., meta-analysis (J Pers Med 2022; PMC8874476)

categories.management: Repeat urine cytology (preferably a fresh voided or instrumented sample); cystoscopy as clinically indicated.
criteria: Voided urine: volume below ~25–30 mL is suboptimal; very low cellularity.
Instrumented: fewer than ~20 urothelial cells/10 HPF (ThinPrep guidance).
Any atypical/suspicious/HGUC cells make the sample adequate.

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – scant cellularity
diagnoses.final: Unsatisfactory/Non-diagnostic for evaluation of high-grade urothelial carcinoma – scant cellularity.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat urine sample (≥25–30 mL, fresh, ideally not first morning) recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Non-diagnostic

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – obscuring blood/degeneration
diagnoses.final: Unsatisfactory/Non-diagnostic – cellular detail obscured by blood/degeneration.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Non-diagnostic

categories.name: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
categories.definition: Benign urothelial, squamous and glandular cells, reactive changes, LGUN-type groups without atypia, and benign findings.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Nikas IP et al., meta-analysis (J Pers Med 2022; PMC8874476)

criteria: Benign urothelial cells, umbrella cells, benign urothelial tissue fragments and groups (incl. from instrumentation/stones).
Reactive/degenerated cells, polyoma (decoy) cells, treatment effects (BCG, chemo), ileal conduit cells.
N:C ratio <0.5 in non-superficial cells (TPS 2.0 AUC threshold >0.5).

diagnoses.name: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Benign urothelial tissue fragments / groups
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Benign urothelial tissue fragments present.
diagnoses.comment: Seen with instrumentation, stones or low-grade neoplasia; not diagnostic of LGUN without cystoscopic lesion.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Polyomavirus (BK) cytopathic effect (decoy cells)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Polyomavirus cytopathic effect present.
diagnoses.comment: Decoy cells with ground-glass intranuclear inclusions; in transplant patients consider BK viral load testing.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Reactive urothelial cells (lithiasis, catheter, infection)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Reactive urothelial changes.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Treatment effect (BCG, intravesical chemotherapy, radiation)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Changes consistent with therapy effect.
diagnoses.comment: BCG may show granulomas; mitomycin/radiation cause enlarged cells with preserved N:C ratio.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Ileal conduit / neobladder urine
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Degenerated enteric-type cells consistent with conduit urine.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Squamous cells / organisms (Trichomonas, Schistosoma, fungi)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). [Squamous cells / organism] noted.
diagnoses.comment: Schistosoma haematobium ova increase SCC risk.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Low-grade urothelial neoplasm (second-line diagnosis)
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Findings may represent a low-grade urothelial neoplasm (LGUN) [only with fibrovascular cores or a known cystoscopic lesion].
diagnoses.comment: In TPS 2.0 LGUN is no longer a separate primary category; it is reported as a second-line diagnosis under NHGUC. Cystoscopic/histological correlation. Reported ROHM for LGUN 0–44% (TPS 2.0 table, via JCTP 2022 review); pooled 12.5% (Nikas et al. 2022).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

diagnoses.name: Seminal vesicle cells
diagnoses.final: Negative for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (NHGUC). Seminal vesicle cells present.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – NHGUC

categories.name: Atypical urothelial cells
categories.definition: Non-superficial, non-degenerated urothelial cells with N:C ratio >0.5 AND one of: hyperchromasia, irregular nuclear membranes, irregular coarse chromatin.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Nikas IP et al., meta-analysis (J Pers Med 2022; PMC8874476)

categories.management: Repeat cytology, cystoscopy ± biopsy, ancillary tests (UroVysion FISH) where available; expected AUC rate 5–15% (TPS 2.0).
criteria: Plus one of: nuclear hyperchromasia (vs umbrella cells), irregular nuclear contours, irregular coarse clumped chromatin.
Do not use for degenerated cells or reactive changes alone.

diagnoses.name: Atypical urothelial cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical urothelial cells (AUC).
diagnoses.comment: Rare urothelial cells with increased N:C ratio and hyperchromasia are seen, insufficient for suspicious for HGUC. Cystoscopy/repeat cytology suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – AUC

categories.name: Suspicious for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
categories.definition: Urothelial cells with N:C ≥0.7 and moderate–severe hyperchromasia plus at least one of irregular membranes or coarse chromatin, but fewer than the threshold for HGUC.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Nikas IP et al., meta-analysis (J Pers Med 2022; PMC8874476)

categories.management: Cystoscopy with biopsy; upper tract evaluation if bladder negative.
criteria: Required: N:C ratio ≥0.7 and moderate to severe hyperchromasia.
Plus one of: markedly irregular nuclear membranes or coarse/clumped chromatin.
Number of such cells below HGUC threshold (<5–10 in voided).

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for high-grade urothelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (SHGUC).
diagnoses.comment: Few cells with high N:C ratio and hyperchromasia; cystoscopy with biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – SHGUC

categories.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma
categories.definition: Includes invasive HGUC and urothelial carcinoma in situ; ≥5–10 cells meeting criteria.

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Nikas IP et al., meta-analysis (J Pers Med 2022; PMC8874476)

criteria: N:C ≥0.7, moderate–severe hyperchromasia, markedly irregular nuclear membranes, coarse clumped chromatin.
Cellular pleomorphism, single cells, necrosis, mitoses; minimum ~5–10 abnormal cells in voided specimens.
Variants (squamous/glandular differentiation, micropapillary, plasmacytoid) may be mentioned.

diagnoses.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC).
diagnoses.comment: Cystoscopy with biopsy and upper urinary tract evaluation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

diagnoses.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma with squamous/glandular differentiation
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC), with squamous differentiation.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

diagnoses.name: High-grade urothelial carcinoma, micropapillary/plasmacytoid features
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC) with [micropapillary / plasmacytoid] features.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

diagnoses.name: Urothelial carcinoma in situ (cytologic correlate)
diagnoses.final: Positive for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (HGUC).
diagnoses.comment: Cytology cannot distinguish CIS from invasive HGUC; cystoscopy and biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – HGUC

categories.name: Other malignancies, primary and secondary

rom.source: TPS 2.0 book (Springer 2022) via JCTP 2022 review Table 1
Nikas IP et al., meta-analysis (J Pers Med 2022; PMC8874476)

criteria: Primary: squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma (incl. urachal), small cell carcinoma, sarcoma.
Secondary: prostate, colorectal, cervical, renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, melanoma.

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Exclude HGUC with squamous differentiation and extension from cervix.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Other malignancies

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma (primary/urachal or metastatic)
diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – adenocarcinoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Other malignancies

diagnoses.name: Small cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – small cell (high-grade neuroendocrine) carcinoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Other malignancies

diagnoses.name: Prostatic adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – adenocarcinoma, consistent with prostatic origin.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Other malignancies

diagnoses.name: Renal cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – carcinoma, consistent with renal cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Other malignancies

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma / melanoma / other metastasis
diagnoses.final: Positive for malignancy – [type].
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: The Paris System 2.0 – Other malignancies

extra.title: Changes in TPS 2.0
items: LGUN removed as a primary category – now a second-line diagnosis within NHGUC.
AUC: N:C 0.5–0.7 plus one minor criterion; expected AUC rate 5–15%.
'Atypical urothelial cells' requires one secondary feature (hyperchromasia, irregular membranes, or coarse chromatin).
LGUN and NHGUC clarified; upper tract and ileal conduit chapters; ancillary tests chapter.

references: Wojcik EM, Kurtycz DFI, Rosenthal DL (eds). The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology. 2nd ed. Springer, 2022.
The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: An Updated Review. J Clin Transl Pathol. 2022 (doi 10.14218/jctp.2022.00035).
Nikas IP, et al. The Paris System for Reporting Urinary Cytology: a meta-analysis. J Pers Med. 2022 (PMC8874476).
